name: faq-answer-depth-gutter
title: FAQ Answer Depth Gutter
description: An FAQ whose left gutter is a real measurement instrument: each question's tick is drawn proportional to the exact pixel height its answer will occupy, so the column reads as a bar chart of answer length at rest and opening a question is the tick growing to the number it was always predicting.
useWhen: Pick faq-answer-depth-gutter when the reader should be able to tell, before clicking anything, which answers are one-liners and which are three paragraphs — the resting gutter is a truthful bar chart of answer length. accordion-latch is the better pick when the closed state itself should read as mechanically shut rather than as a measurement, and truncation-word-count is for expanding a single clamped block of prose in place rather than a list of questions.
instruction: Build <FaqDepthGutter items allowMultiple? defaultOpen? className?> where items is {id, question, answer: ReactNode}[]. STRUCTURE: each item is a flex row of a 3px gutter column and a body containing a real <button data-faq-trigger aria-expanded aria-controls={panelId}> inside an <h3>, plus a <div data-faq-panel data-open role="region" aria-labelledby={triggerId}> panel. MEASUREMENT is the whole component: one offscreen mirror div (position:absolute; left:-9999px; visibility:hidden; pointer-events:none; aria-hidden) renders every answer once, and in a useLayoutEffect the mirror is sized to the answer column's real width — taken from a zero-height probe row whose body cell sits in the same flex geometry — and each answer's offsetHeight is recorded into a Map<id, naturalHeight>. A ResizeObserver on that probe re-measures the whole map ONLY when the column width moves by more than WIDTH_EPSILON = 2px, and document.fonts.ready triggers one extra pass so the bars are not drawn from fallback font metrics; it never runs per frame. THE MECHANIC: the tick's resting height is clamp(REST_MIN 6, naturalHeight * REST_RATIO 0.22, REST_MAX 64) px in --border ink — a scaled-down but truthful preview, which is what makes the resting column legible as a bar chart of answer length with zero interaction. On pointerenter or focus of the trigger the tick eases to min(naturalHeight, PREVIEW_MAX 260) px over 220ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) and shifts to color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 55%, transparent): the page has not moved yet, but you can see how far it is about to. On open, the SAME cached number drives both halves at once — the panel animates height 0 -> naturalHeight over OPEN_MS 260ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) and on transitionend is set to height:auto (so later reflow or a text-wrap change stays correct), while the tick locks at exactly naturalHeight in solid --accent. Promise and delivery are literally the same measurement. Closing reverses: height:auto is pinned back to the measured px, a forced reflow (void el.offsetHeight) commits it, then it eases to 0 over CLOSE_MS 200ms and the tick relaxes to its 22% resting height. allowMultiple defaults to false — opening one closes the previous, and the outgoing collapse and incoming expansion are scheduled on the SAME requestAnimationFrame callback so the net page displacement is one continuous movement instead of two competing transitions. ACCESSIBILITY: real button semantics, so Tab/Enter/Space are native and there is no keydown handler; aria-expanded on the trigger, aria-controls to the panel id, aria-labelledby back to the trigger; the panel receives the `hidden` attribute only after the close transition ends, so a screen reader never sees a half-collapsed region; data-open is exposed on both row and panel for probing; the trigger carries a visible :focus-visible outline in --accent at 3px offset. REDUCED MOTION: prefers-reduced-motion (read via matchMedia with a change listener, not just a media query) skips the hover growth entirely — the tick stays at its resting height — and the panel toggles between 0 and auto with no transition, so nothing can be left stuck mid-animation. TOKENS ONLY: --border for resting ink and row rules, --foreground for questions, --muted for answers and the plus/minus sign, --accent on the tick, on the :focus-visible ring and on the hovered question's text, nowhere else; both themes come out of the same variables. REST STATE: the demo mounts with defaultOpen set to its longest answer, so the idle frame shows both halves of the mechanic at once — several short --border ticks scaled from unopened answers, and one --accent tick locked at the exact height of the answer it delivered. Zero dependencies, no canvas, no external animation library.
